model_disclaimer: Representative benchmark probe of the planned shape. NOT the frozen model architecture and never trained for playing strength.
recommended_legality_rationale: Dense legality is recommended: compact is only +3.7 percent end to end, which does not clear the 5 percent adoption margin robustly, so its padded fixed-capacity representation and the capacity-overflow failure mode it introduces are not justified. Sparse legality should not be forced on later agents. Legality transport costs 10000 bytes/position dense against 504 bytes/position compact at capacity 56. Widening the padding capacity from 56 to 256 changes the compact end-to-end rate by +0.0 percent. At the matched configuration (batch 2048, float16) compact is +5.6 percent on the end-to-end step while its legality+sampling stage alone is 7.5x faster: the encoder dominates the step, so the stage speed-up does not carry through. Priced at the production padding capacity of 128 rather than the pool's observed 56, compact is +5.2 percent against the same dense configuration. Repeatability, 5 interleaved dense/compact pairs at batch 2048, float16, capacity 128: mean +3.7 percent, median +4.1 percent, range +1.0 to +5.1 percent, standard deviation 1.6 percentage points, compact ahead in every pair: True.
recommended_precision_rationale: float16 is recommended: 19.6 percent faster than float32 on the complete inference + legality + sampling path, with greedy-action agreement 0.996 and the legal-set distribution unchanged within tolerance. Ties within 2 percent on speed were broken on agreement with the float32 distribution. Measured: bfloat16: +18.7 percent against float32, stable=True, max legal-probability difference 1.27e-03, greedy agreement 0.941; float16: +19.6 percent against float32, stable=True, max legal-probability difference 1.34e-04, greedy agreement 0.996.
